summary: Predictive autoscaling overprovisioned Dedicated pool overnight (forecast confidence gating not effective)
description:
Issue summary
HelioSearch reports their Dedicated pool scaled up overnight (low traffic period) and stayed near max capacity for ~3 hours, resulting in unexpected spend. They have min/max bounds configured, and predictive scaling enabled (design partner). They expected the forecast confidence gating to prevent aggressive pre-scale when signals are low quality.

Impact
- Customer spend increased for overnight window (unexpected capacity increase).
- No customer-facing outage; some internal concern about predictive scaling trustworthiness.

Customer context
- Customer: HelioSearch (Enterprise / Dedicated)
- Dedicated pool: dp-heliosearch-prod-use1 (A100-80G)
- Config (per customer): min_gpus=8, max_gpus=32, burst_to_max=true, cooldown_scale_up=120s, cooldown_scale_down=600s
- Predictive scaling: enabled via allowlist flag

What happened (customer report)
- 2026-01-27 01:55–02:10 ET: pool scaled from 8 -> 32 GPUs without a corresponding traffic increase.
- 02:10–05:20 ET: held between 28–32 GPUs; QPS remained low.
- 05:25 ET: scaled back down gradually.

Initial triage notes (Support)
- Queue depth and p95 latency were stable/low at the time of the scale-up.
- Autoscaler decision logs show desired_replicas driven primarily by forecast input (reactive inputs would have held at/near min).
- Forecast confidence was recorded as 0.92–0.98 during the window.

Environment / signals
- Region: us-east
- Time window: 2026-01-27 01:30–06:00 ET
- Signals inspected: token_rate, QPS, queue_depth, GPU utilization, forecast_demand, forecast_confidence, clamp_reason

Steps to reproduce (approx)
1) Enable predictive scaling allowlist on a Dedicated pool with bounds (min=8/max=32) and burst_to_max enabled.
2) Provide intermittent/missing token_rate telemetry for a subset of routers (observed around the window).
3) Observe forecast service emitting a high confidence score while predicted demand spikes.
4) Autoscaler blends forecast and reactive and drives desired replicas to max.

Evidence
- Decision logs (redacted): clamp_reason=none, desired_replicas=32, applied_replicas=32, reactive_desired=8, forecast_desired=34, forecast_confidence=0.96
- Telemetry anomaly suspected: token_rate aggregation gaps for dp-heliosearch-prod-use1 between 01:40–02:05 ET.

Working hypothesis
Forecast confidence gating is not correctly penalizing missing/partial telemetry, causing overconfident forecasts overnight. In the blending logic, high confidence allows forecast_desired to dominate even when reactive signals are flat.

Immediate mitigation
- Disable predictive scaling for HelioSearch pool via allowlist flag (revert to reactive-only) while investigation continues.
- Monitor next overnight cycle for stability.

Ask / requested outcome
- Root cause + fix (confidence gating / data quality checks).
- Guidance for customer (what to expect when predictive is enabled; how to interpret confidence).
- Confirm whether credit is appropriate for the overprovisioned window (route to CS/Finance once validated).
comments:
2026-01-28 08:42 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Customer (HelioSearch) reports overnight spend spike: Dedicated pool scaled to max despite low traffic. They’re asking if predictive scaling is “stuck on” and how confidence gating works. Requesting Infra/SRE support to investigate. Attaching timestamps and pool id dp-heliosearch-prod-use1.

Next step: pull scaling decision events + forecast outputs for the window.

2026-01-28 09:10 (Keiko Yamamoto, Infra Autoscaling)
Taking. I can confirm from autoscaler logs: scaling decisions were forecast-driven. Reactive desired was 8 the whole time; forecast desired jumped to 34 (then clamped to 32 by max). Confidence is logged ~0.95.

Mitigation suggestion: disable predictive for this pool via bounded-autoscaling allowlist toggle (customer-specific) until we understand why confidence was high.

2026-01-28 09:25 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Acknowledged. Coordinating with TAM (Liam O'Rourke) to message customer: we’ll temporarily disable predictive and follow up with RCA.

Action: please disable predictive flag for dp-heliosearch-prod-use1 as soon as safe.

2026-01-28 09:41 (Connor O'Brien, Release)
Flag flipped for HelioSearch pool: predictive disabled, reactive-only active. Change logged under bounded-autoscaling allowlist (us-east).

2026-01-28 10:05 (Aisha Bello, SRE)
Reviewed dashboards: no queue growth, utilization low, p95 low during scale-up. Not an SLO event. This looks like forecast pipeline / blending behavior.

Requesting data quality check on forecast inputs: do we have gaps in token_rate/QPS at that time? If inputs missing, confidence should be lower per ADR-0143 intent.

2026-01-28 11:18 (Yara Haddad, Applied ML)
I see a telemetry gap for the pool’s router shard around 01:45–02:00 ET (token_rate aggregation missing for a subset). Our current confidence computation isn’t accounting for “missingness” strongly enough; it can stay high if the model is falling back to seasonal baseline.

Also noticing the seasonal baseline has a recurring 02:00 ET spike from historical data (from a prior load test week). That spike shouldn’t be “high confidence” given current missing inputs.

Proposed fix: add explicit missing-data penalty + require minimum sample coverage before confidence can exceed threshold. Also add a cap on forecast_desired delta when reactive is flat.

2026-01-28 12:03 (Keiko Yamamoto, Infra Autoscaling)
+1. Blending currently treats confidence as authoritative; if it’s high, forecast can dominate. We can add a guardrail: if reactive_desired is at min and queue_depth ~0, limit forecast-driven scale-up to X% per interval unless confidence >= 0.99 AND telemetry coverage healthy.

This aligns with “graceful degradation when predictive signal quality is low” and should prevent maxing out overnight on phantom spikes.

2026-01-29 09:22 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Customer update sent (via Liam): predictive scaling disabled temporarily, we’re investigating telemetry gaps + confidence gating. Customer asks whether they should lower max to avoid spend surprises while predictive is in pilot. They’d like a recommendation.

Request: provide interim guidance for HelioSearch (max bounds, cooldowns) and whether we can offer credit for the overprovisioned window.

2026-01-29 10:10 (Rishi Malhotra, FP&A)
If we confirm this was platform-driven overprovisioning (not customer traffic), we typically offer a usage credit for the incremental capacity window. Please estimate GPU-hours attributable to the incident and route through CS (Rachel Kim) for approval.

2026-01-30 14:37 (Keiko Yamamoto, Infra Autoscaling)
RCA (prelim): forecast confidence overstated during telemetry gaps; seasonal baseline contained an artifact spike at ~02:00 ET from historical load test week. Blending respected forecast due to confidence, causing scale to max (within customer bounds).

Fix plan:
1) Forecast service: add coverage checks + missingness penalty; ensure confidence cannot be >0.8 when coverage below threshold.
2) Autoscaler blending: add guardrail on forecast-driven ramp when reactive signals indicate idle.
3) Observability: alert when confidence high + observed demand flat for >N minutes.

Tracking under ENG-2844/2845 work; will coordinate PR(s).

2026-02-03 09:05 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Customer confirms overnight since disabling predictive: no unexpected scaling; spend consistent. They still want predictive benefits, but only if confidence is explainable and safe.

Please advise if/when we can re-enable for them (post-fix) and what monitoring we’ll have in place.

2026-02-05 16:20 (Keiko Yamamoto, Infra Autoscaling)
We’ll keep predictive disabled for HelioSearch until:
- confidence coverage check is deployed to prod AND
- autoscaler guardrail is enabled behind the same allowlist.

Support can close this as Resolved with mitigation in place. Follow-up actions:
- Re-enable only after fixed build + one monitored overnight window.
- CS to process credit request once Support provides GPU-hour delta estimate.

(References: ADR-0143 predictive blending; runbook for autoscaling anomalies updated with ‘high confidence + low demand’ diagnostic.)

2026-02-05 16:45 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Resolution: Predictive scaling disabled for dp-heliosearch-prod-use1 (reactive-only). No further overnight overprovision observed. RCA points to telemetry gaps + seasonal artifact causing high confidence forecast. Fixes tracked with Eng; credit request in progress via CS/FP&A.

Closing ticket; will reopen if issue recurs after re-enable.
resolution: Mitigated by disabling predictive scaling allowlist for HelioSearch Dedicated pool; investigation identified confidence gating/data-quality shortcomings and a seasonal baseline artifact. Engineering fixes tracked in linked eng work; customer to be re-enabled after fixes and monitored validation. Credit request pending via CS/FP&A.
next_actions: Estimate incremental GPU-hours for 2026-01-27 02:00–05:20 ET and route to CS/FP&A for credit approval.
Add forecast telemetry coverage threshold and missingness penalty before allowing high confidence.
Add autoscaler guardrail limiting forecast-driven ramp when reactive indicates idle (queue_depth low/util low).
Add alert: high forecast_confidence + flat observed demand sustained; page to oncall only if repeated / multiple pools.
